The cycle was in week 2 of 5 on the focus Homestead & Off-Grid Tech, but zero articles matched it. The pipeline needs at least 4, so it fell back to the base theme selection, Gear, Gadgets & Practical Tech, with the theme feed Repair Culture & Practical Tech. Of 78 articles loaded, 19 were on theme and 58 were bonus. After 65 were removed as duplicates, 3 were released by focus routing and 7 were held for other focus days. The listener got the standing theme for the day, not the week's planned focus, and nothing on the homestead theme aired.

The held queue shows what the routing sent to other days. Seven items were held, four of them for Discovery, Health & How Science Works and Economic Development, and the earliest release date is 2026-11-26. Nothing was lost, but the focus cycle will not carry the homestead story unless homestead articles arrive on their own.

Change: if zero-match weeks recur, check the homestead feed sources in the focus configuration before the cycle starts, not after it has already fallen back.

Roundup built from 18 stories; 39 cut by the airtime budget

The roundup pool held 18 stories, 13 on theme and 5 local. All 5 local stories aired, and the roundup opened on local news. The airtime budget cut 39 stories from the pool; by design those can resurface on a better-matched day. The short-script result is the tension to watch: the first draft came in at 2738 words against a target of 3400, was sent back for one expand pass, and shipped at 3255 words. That is under target but above the short-episode threshold, so no alert fired.

Citations were matched on 14 of 18 roundup stories and 2 of 4 deep-dive stories, so the deep dive is the weaker of the two on sourcing.

Change: none for the budget. If the citation gap on deep dives repeats, inspect the four deep-dive source links in the script stage.

Weather came from Environment Canada; Open-Meteo did not respond

Open-Meteo did not answer, so the weather segment used the Environment Canada forecast. Williams Lake was reported, and Horsefly got no figure. Listeners in Horsefly heard no forecast for their own town.

One TTS take came back shorter than its word count predicted and was retried. The retry was still short, so the longer of the two takes was kept and nothing was dropped from the episode. The retry count is one take, not a run of problems.

item.dc:creator: Cariboo Signals Reviews
item.description:
Theme: Cariboo Local Affairs. Run 44883218714.

▲
Shipped, needs a look1 thing to look at before tomorrow's run.

What to do

  1. script/weather fell back. Search the run log for Degraded 'script/weather' and decide whether the fallback is acceptable or the cause needs fixing.
    degrade() row: Open-Meteo did not answer — the episode airs with no weather check and no weather credit

What happened

Two of three runs were fallbacks, and the primary run was not the one that published the episode

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and completed at 1:33 AM Pacific with a success conclusion. Fallback 1 (2:05 AM Pacific) also completed successfully. Fallback 2 at 3:05 AM Pacific is the run writing this review and is still in progress. Each run's url is in the run record above, so the maintainer can check which run produced the published artifacts.

Weather did not run. Open-Meteo did not answer, so the episode aired with no weather check and no weather credit. This is the one degradation in the run, and it removed a segment from the listener's episode entirely rather than shortening it.

The script came in under target and shipped under target

The first draft was 2,407 words against a 3,400-word target. It was sent back for one expand pass, and the shipped script is 3,100 words. The episode is still 300 words short of target, which is the thin-day case the pipeline tolerates. The episode's word count is well above the length the pipeline counts as short under SHORT_EPISODE_WORDS.

The cold open was skipped because it ran 91 words, which exceeded the length limit. Listeners heard the episode without it. Consider raising the cold-open word limit if this recurs on normal nights, since skipping it removes the framing the show normally opens with.

Local stories filled the roundup but only two theme stories made it in

The roundup pool kept 18 stories: 16 local and 2 theme. Of 39 local stories available, 16 aired. The roundup opened local, and the deep dives all led with local subjects, with one Cariboo deep dive. Six on-theme candidates were not used. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) cut 55 stories from the roundup pool; those stories remain eligible for a later, better-matched day.

Theme loading, by contrast, was not the constraint: 52 theme articles loaded against 51 bonus articles. The bottleneck was airtime, not the feed. If the theme should carry more of the roundup, raise its share of NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT rather than widening the pool.

Thirteen of eighteen roundup citations matched the aired script

Roundup citations matched 12 of 18, and deep-dive citations matched 3 of 5. Five roundup citations and two deep-dive citations did not align with what was aired. Check the citation alignment step against the storyboard before trusting those segments' source attributions.

The text-to-speech canary timed out and OpenAI rendered the whole episode

Two of the short TTS takes were retried, and both retries came back short again. The longer take of each was kept, so no content was dropped, but the audio for those two takes is shorter than their word count predicts. This is a single observation about two takes, not a missing segment.
